paid_market_gaps.gap: Small municipalities (Hodonín, est. CZK 1.5M) tender full PAM delivery and had to re-issue the tender
Tenders scored 100% on lowest price favour bundled integrator bids; no product differentiation is rewarded
Lithuanian-only tender documents and 60-month service scope need local integrator partners, not direct vendor sales
Czech NIS2 lower-regime decree brings many small entities under access-control duties with limited budgets

wtp_evidence: Public buyers budget real money for PAM: a regional hospital estimates CZK 13.2M over 60 months, a town CZK 1.5M; but awards go on lowest price, squeezing margins.
bundling_note: Entra ID P2 includes select PIM for cloud roles, but on-prem session recording, vaulting and rotation that these tenders specify remain paid products.
summary: Procurement is real but crowded and integrator-led, judged on lowest price. A startup could only win as a cheap, quickly deployable, EU-sovereign PAM sold through local integrators to small NIS2-regulated public bodies; thin margins.
